name: Hovatter's Wildlife Zoo
distance: About 26 miles from Oakland, four miles between Kingwood and Reedsville. Roughly 45 minutes, and over the state line.
blurb: A family-run zoo in rural Preston County with over thirty species: chimpanzees, grizzlies, a giraffe, a herd of fallow deer that walks right up to the fence, and a walk-in room full of parakeets. You can feed some of the animals. There's a gift shop, a snack area, restrooms and somewhere to picnic.
season: Open seven days a week, 10am to 6pm, last admission 5pm. Open on all holidays. The 2026 season opened 11 April.

admission.note: Adults 13-64 $15.99. Seniors 65+ and military with ID $12.99. Children 3-12 $11.99. Two and under free. Season passes: $70 adult, $65 senior or military, $60 child.

onSite.label: Feeding them
onSite.note: Feed runs $1 to $5 depending on what you buy, and they take credit. You don't need to hunt for an ATM first.

warnings: This is in West Virginia, not Garrett County. Everything else on this site is Maryland.
Last admission is 5pm, an hour before closing. Worth knowing on a 45-minute drive.

sources.label: Hovatter's Wildlife Zoo: the zoo's own brochure, collected on site
sources.note: Printed brochure picked up at the gate on 4 August 2026. Gives park hours (7 days, 10am to 6pm, last admission 5pm, open all holidays), the address, phone, and the USDA license. Admission and season pass prices are from the posted price list inside.

sources.label: West Virginia Zoo: official site
sources.note: The operator. Gives the 11 April 2026 opening, the 34th season, the phone number, and the species list. Publishes no admission prices or daily hours on the front page.

sources.label: West Virginia Zoo: directions
sources.note: Confirms Hovatter's Wildlife Zoo and West Virginia Zoo are the same place, gives the address, and routes visitors from Oakland, Maryland — though it describes the zoo as east of Oakland when it is west.

verifiedSource: Visited, and read off the zoo's own brochure on site

reports.what: Restrooms, a snack area and somewhere to picnic. You can feed some of the animals — feed is $1 to $5 and they take credit — and there's a gift shop. The paths take a stroller. Prices and hours photographed on site.

outstanding: Confirm the closing date of the 2026 season.
Confirm whether it's walk-through throughout, and roughly how long a full visit takes.

verdict.text: Better than it has any right to be for the price. Chimps, grizzlies, a giraffe, a tortoise the size of a coffee table, and a room of parakeets that lands on you. Feed is a few dollars and they take credit. Watch the 5pm last admission, because the gate says six.

photos.alt: A very large tortoise resting on bare earth beside a wire fence, with a paved path and trees behind it.
photos.caption: One of the tortoises, out by the path rather than behind glass.

photos.caption: The flamingo enclosure, mid-afternoon in early August.

photos.caption: This one came over on its own. The fence is wire, so you end up nose to nose.

photos.caption: Goat Mountain. The goats work the fence line, so they'll find you before you find them.

name: Dans Mountain State Park
distance: Over the Allegany County line at Lonaconing, about an hour from Oakland.
address: 17410 Recreation Area Road SW, Lonaconing, MD 21539
kind: State park with a public pool
blurb: 481 acres on a sixteen-mile ridge, and the reason to drive out is the pool: heated, with a water slide, staffed by certified lifeguards and fully accessible. Also a fishing pond, a recycled-tire playground, pavilions and trails.
season: The pool runs Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day, 11am to 6pm.

admission.note: Not confirmed. The guide describes the pool and names no price.

onSite.label: The pool
onSite.note: Heated, with a water slide, renovated in 2023. Refreshments sold at the entrance to the pool building.

onSite.label: Group camping
onSite.note: The Hill Run Group Campsite takes up to 40 people, reservable May through September. A large pavilion with a fireplace and electric outlets. Showers and potable water are NOT available; there is a portable bathroom.

onSite.label: Pavilions
onSite.note: Three: Mountain Top, Pythian, and Water Station Run, the last with a view over the fishing pond. April to October, 888-432-2267 or parkreservations.maryland.gov.

onSite.label: Trails
onSite.note: The 4.5-mile Lonacona Loop, built 2023, gains 650 feet over rocky ground. The Dye School Trail makes a one-mile option and passes the foundation of a one-room schoolhouse from the late 1800s.

website.label: Maryland DNR: Garrett County state parks

warnings: This is Allegany County, not Garrett. It appears in the county's own parks guide anyway, which is why it's here.
Pool hours change with weather, staffing and maintenance. Ring 301-895-5453 before driving.
The group campsite has no showers and no drinking water.

sources.label: Explore 2026 Garrett County State Parks (printed guide)
sources.note: The Maryland Park Service's own 2026 printed guide to the Garrett County parks, photographed page by page. Primary: published by the operator.

outstanding: Confirm the 2026 pool opening and closing dates.
Confirm whether the park itself charges entry outside the pool.

name: Blackwater Falls State Park
distance: Over the West Virginia line at Davis, in Tucker County.
kind: State park with a lodge, cabins and a waterfall
blurb: A 57-foot waterfall the color of strong tea — the park says that's tannic acid off fallen hemlock and red spruce needles, not silt. There are two ways to see it: more than 200 steps down a boardwalk, or a quarter-mile of pavement to a second overlook. Same falls, very different walk.
season: The park is open 6am to 10pm. The campground runs 28 April to 31 October.

admission.note: Not confirmed. West Virginia State Parks doesn't state an entrance fee on this park's page, and doesn't state that there isn't one either. Ring 304-259-5216 before you budget for it.

onSite.label: Blackwater Falls Boardwalk Trail
onSite.note: A quarter of a mile from the Trading Post parking area to a stone patio, then a boardwalk of more than 200 steps down to an observation deck beside the falls. Down is the easy half.

onSite.label: Gentle Trail
onSite.note: A quarter of a mile, paved, from the parking area across from the maintenance area to an observation deck overlooking the falls. The park calls it a short paved path and does not call it wheelchair accessible — those aren't the same claim, so ring first if that's what decides your trip.

onSite.label: The sled run
onSite.note: The park calls it the longest of its kind on the East Coast, with a Magic Carpet conveyor that carries you and the sled back up. Dates and prices aren't published on the park page.

onSite.label: Trails, twenty-odd of them
onSite.note: Easy ones include Balanced Rock (1 mi), Balsam Fir (1.5 mi) and Red Spruce (1.25 mi). Moderate: Elakala (0.5 mi), Yellow Birch (1 mi), Allegheny (1.2 mi). Hardest are Lindy Point (0.3 mi) and Cherry Lane (1 mi).

onSite.label: Lodging
onSite.note: A lodge, cabins and a campground. The campground season is the only one of the three with published dates.

website.label: West Virginia State Parks: Blackwater Falls

warnings: This is West Virginia, not Maryland. Different state park system, different rules, and a Maryland park pass is no good here.
More than 200 steps down to the falls overlook, and the same 200 back up. If that's a problem, the Gentle Trail goes to a different overlook without them.
No entrance fee is published either way. Ring 304-259-5216 rather than assuming.

sources.label: West Virginia State Parks: Blackwater Falls State Park
sources.note: The operator. Gives the Blackwater Lodge Rd address, the phone number, 6am-10pm hours, the campground season of 28 April to 31 October, the lodge and cabins, and the description of the falls as a 57-foot cascade tinted by tannic acid from hemlock and red spruce. Publishes no entrance fee, no restroom detail and no pet policy of its own.

sources.label: West Virginia State Parks: Blackwater Falls trails
sources.note: The operator. Gives the boardwalk trail at 0.25 miles from the Trading Post parking area with more than 200 steps to the observation deck, the Gentle Trail at 0.25 miles paved from the parking area across from the maintenance area, and the full trail list with lengths and difficulty grades.

sources.note: The operator, statewide. "Dogs and cats are the only pets permitted in state parks and forests." and pets must be leashed and restrained. It does not say where in a park they're prohibited.
